2015_083_070715mtg.paragraph: Agenda packet for the Troy School District Board of Education regular meeting of July 7, 2015 at the Administration Building, 4400 Livernois, with the consent-agenda minutes of the June 2 and June 16, 2015 meetings attached. The headline action is the extension of Superintendent Dr. Rich Machesky's contract through June 30, 2018 after a HIGHLY EFFECTIVE first-year evaluation, carrying a 3.5% base salary increase and a Board-authorized $5000 bonus. Also before the Board are a $94,383.98 office-furnishings award to Interior Environments for Boulan Park and Larson Middle Schools, MHSAA membership, a Troy High/Athens boys' ice hockey cooperative team, and a revised Athletic Code of Conduct.

Meeting
Regular meeting of the Troy Board of Education, July 7, 2015, 7:00 PM, Administration Building, 4400 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098. Meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) and viewable at http://vimeo.com/troyschools.

Consent Agenda (Item 5)
Minutes of the June 2, 2015 Board of Education meeting, the June 16, 2015 special meeting, the June 16, 2015 closed session, and the June 16, 2015 Board workshop.

Personnel (Item 6)
A. New hire: Michael Denyes, 1.0 FTE Counselor, Smith/Boulan Park Middle Schools, probationary contract for 2015-2016. B.A. Oakland University, Rochester, May 2010 (Psychology, Anthropology); M.A. Oakland University, December 2012 (School Counselor); Michigan School Counselor Certificate, January 2013; Counselor, Holly Area Schools, August 2013 - June 2015; Guest Counselor, PESG, Caledonia, February 2013 - June 2013; resident of Troy, Michigan.
B. Superintendent's contract extension: the Board rated Dr. Richard Machesky HIGHLY EFFECTIVE for his first year, citing the One Troy concept, a customer service mindset in Central Office, successfully negotiated labor contracts, and continued fiscal strength. The Board authorized a $5000 bonus, a 3.5% base salary increase, and an extension from July 1, 2015 through June 30, 2018, without tenure in the administrative position.

Curriculum (Item 7)
A. MHSAA membership resolution enrolling the district's six (6) secondary schools, City of Troy, County of Oakland, effective August 1, 2015 through July 31, 2016.
B. Cooperative team agreement for Boys' Ice Hockey between Troy High School (primary) and Athens High School (secondary) for the 2015-16 and 2016-17 school years.
C. Revised Code of Conduct for Student Athletes (Revised December 2004; Revised July 2015), twelve sections covering eligibility, awards, amateur status, attendance, travel, uniforms, substance use, off-season programs, supplemental rules and appeals.

Business (Item 8)
Office furnishings for Boulan Park and Larson Middle Schools. Invitations went to seven potential bidders; two responded. Recommended award to Interior Environments, funded from the 2014 Capital Projects Fund.

June 2, 2015 minutes highlights
Held at Athens High School as Youth Recognition Night with approximately 300 in the audience; President Philippart presided, with Edmunds, Fleming, Miletti and Schmidt present and Hauff and Underwood absent. Resolutions adopted 5-0 included 15-051 (new hire Kerry Collins), 15-052 (Jordan Harris, Assistant Superintendent, Employee Services, effective August 3, 2015), 15-053 (Erica Rolack, Elementary Principal, July 1, 2015), 15-054 (Elementary ELD materials), 15-055 (Michigan Council for Arts and Cultural Affairs grant), 15-056 (public hearing on the 2015-2016 budget set for June 23, 2015 at the Troy School District Services Building, 4420 Livernois Road), 15-057 (roof replacement awarded to J.D. Candler Roofing, $341,400.00), 15-058 (Sodexo Management, Inc. food service renewal), 15-059 (point of sale system to Business Machine Company, $37,401.00) and 15-060 (paid lunch price adjustment reflecting a $0.15 increase).

June 16, 2015 meetings
The special meeting appointed Kristine Griffor Assistant Superintendent, Elementary Instruction (15.061), approved the Director of ELD, Federal Grants and State Assessments recommendation for Silagy (15-062), ratified the TESPA tentative agreement of June 5, 2015, and adopted 15-063 to enter closed session on the superintendent evaluation, all 7-0. The workshop that evening covered an Innovations presentation, Summer Success Academy grades 3 and 6, Michigan Merit Curriculum, district property, and a budget update including millage renewal.

Board meeting agenda packet for the Troy School District Board of Education regular meeting of July 7, 2015, convened at 7:00 PM in the Administration Building, 4400 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098 (248.823.4000). The notice states that Board meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) every Monday and Wednesday at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m. when school is in session, and are viewable online at http://vimeo.com/troyschools. The agenda runs: Pledge of Allegiance; Recognition; Additions and Deletions; Public Communication (agenda items); General Consent Agenda; Personnel; Curriculum; Business; Public Communication (non-agenda items); Other; Adjournment.

CONSENT AGENDA (5). Items A through D are the minutes of the June 2, 2015 Board of Education meeting, the June 16, 2015 Special Board of Education Meeting, the June 16, 2015 Closed Session Meeting, and the June 16, 2015 Board of Education Workshop.

JUNE 2, 2015 REGULAR MEETING MINUTES (Athens High School). President Philippart called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. Present in addition to Dr. Philippart were Board members Edmunds, Fleming, Miletti and Schmidt; Mr. Hauff and Ms. Underwood were absent. Also present were Superintendent Machesky; administrators Kerry Birmingham, Ryan Brinks, Jerry Cottone, Lara Dixon, Mark Dziatczak, Tim Fulcher, Mary Haezebrouck, Larry Lobert and Rick West; and approximately 300 members of the audience. The evening was Youth Recognition Night. Mike Jolly and the Board recognized All-State athletes for winter sports including Ellen Barker, Camille Bedford, Zachary Chen (Boys Swim), Soumeeka Koneru, Kaylee Lee, Julia Meng, Anjali Munasinghe, Daphne Samuel, Hye-Kyung Seo, Bhavya Sukhavasi, Amishi Taneja, John Van Hoef (Boys Basketball), Katie Ward and Christina Xu. The 2014-2015 Synchronized Swim Team was honored as State Champions, each member receiving a commemorative plaque, with students from Troy High and Athens including Monica Alluri, Priya Bandstra, Haya Beydoun, Michelle Cai, Joy Goldschmidt, Yejin Kim, Angela Li, Anna Nichols, Sabina Ravindran, Anisha Shukla and Kathleen Young. Senior scholar athletes from winter and spring sports who maintained a 3.5 cumulative grade point average were acknowledged, a roster including Max Adamo, Rajesh Anand, Ryan Bean, Melissa Doozan, Michael Fisher, Jacob Howard, Joseph Jackson, Ryan Melotik, Jesse Nahhat, Corey Svrcina, Robert Urban and Nikhill Yedulla. The Troy Education Association was recognized for sponsoring a hole at the Tony Spagnola Memorial Golf Classic, the primary fundraiser for the Troy Foundation for Educational Excellence, held Friday, June 19th; Foundation representative Rich Maziasz accepted the donation. Dozens of academic competitions were described, among them the Alaska Wilderness League Arctic Bookmark Contest, the American Mathematics Competitions, Business Professionals of America, the Chemistry Olympiad, the Michigan China Quiz Bowl, the DAFT Michigan Student Film Festival in its 47th year, where an Athens student won Best in the State of Michigan/Best in Show for the documentary "STEM Powered: Fostering Curiosity", DECA at the Amway Hotel in Grand Rapids, Destination Imagination, FIRST Robotics, Future Problem Solving Program International, the Governor's Traveling Art Show, HOSA, the Intel International Science and Engineering Fair, the 19th annual Jackie Robinson Art, Essay and Poetry Contest won at middle school level by a Boulan Park student, a Japanese Speech Contest held March 28th at Novi Civic Center where a student won first place in Michigan and a $300 flight voucher, MATHCOUNTS, the Math Kangaroo Olympiad of March 19th, Math Madness, the Michigan Brain Bee at Michigan State University, Michigan Green Schools (Larson Middle School achieved "Emerald" status), the Michigan Mathematics League, the Michigan Youth Arts Festival, MIFA Forensics, the MIT INSPIRE Research Essay National Competition, the MSBOA All-State Band, the National French, German, Japanese and Spanish exams, the National History Bee, National Scholastic Art and Writing Awards, the Purple Comet Math Contest, Robofest, the Rocket City Math League, the Scholastic Star Reader Essay and TombQuest Hieroglyph contests won by a Leonard Elementary student, the Science and Engineering Fair of Metro Detroit at Cobo Hall, Science Olympiad, where the Baker Bobcats finished 4th among 48 qualifying teams, the Siemens Competition, the State Orchestra Festival at Sterling Heights High School, the Stockholm Junior Water Prize, Troy High's Symphonic Orchestra winning the Judge's Honor Award at the National Adjudicators Invitational Grand National Festival, Toshiba ExploraVision, the USA Biology Olympiad, in which 12 Troy High semifinalists placed in the top 10% of the 7,766 students who took the exam nationwide, the Verizon Innovative App Challenge and the WordMasters Challenge.

June 2 resolutions, each adopted Yes 5, No 0 with Hauff and Underwood absent: 15-051, moved by Mr. Schmidt and supported by Mrs. Fleming, approving the personnel recommendation, new hire Kerry Collins. 15-052, moved by Mrs. Fleming and supported by Mrs. Edmunds, issuing a two-year probationary administrative contract without tenure to Mr. Jordan Harris as Assistant Superintendent, Employee Services, effective August 3, 2015. 15-053, moved by Mrs. Edmunds and supported by Mr. Miletti, approving Ms. Erica Rolack as Elementary Principal as of July 1, 2015. 15-054, moved by Mrs. Fleming and supported by Mr. Schmidt, adopting the recommended Elementary ELD instructional materials for the 2015-2016 school year. 15-055, moved by Mr. Miletti and supported by Mrs. Edmunds, approving a Michigan Council for Arts and Cultural Affairs Project Support grant for instrumental music. 15-056, moved by Ms. Edmunds and supported by Mrs. Fleming, resolving that a public hearing on the proposed 2015-2016 budget be held June 23, 2015 at a regular Board meeting beginning at 7:00 p.m. at the Troy School District Services Building, 4420 Livernois Road, Troy 48098; the notice must be published at least six (6) days before the hearing, must include in 11-point bold-faced type the statement that THE PROPERTY TAX MILLAGE RATE PROPOSED TO BE LEVIED TO SUPPORT THE PROPOSED BUDGET WILL BE A SUBJECT OF THIS HEARING, and copies of the proposed budget would be available at the Administration Building, 4400 Livernois, from 8:00 a.m. until 5:00 p.m., Wednesday, June 17, 2015 through Tuesday, June 23, 2015. 15-057, moved by Mr. Schmidt and supported by Mrs. Edmunds, awarding the bid for roof replacement at the Administration and Services buildings to J.D. Candler Roofing in the amount of $341,400.00 as an expenditure of the 2014 Capital Projects Fund. 15-058, moved by Mrs. Fleming and supported by Mr. Miletti, authorizing administration to approve the food services contract renewal with Sodexo Management, Inc. for 2015/2016. 15-059, moved by Mr. Miletti and supported by Mrs. Edmunds, awarding the Point of Sale System contract to Business Machine Company in the amount of $37,401.00 as an expenditure of the 2014-2015 Food Services Fund. 15-060, moved by Mr. Schmidt and supported by Mr. Miletti, adopting paid lunch prices for 2015-2016 under Section 205 of the Healthy, Hunger-Free Kids Act of 2010 and the USDA Food and Nutrition Service paid lunch equity tool, reflecting a $0.15 cent increase from the previous year. The price table is printed as: 2015-2016 K-5 Lunch Price $2.40 student / $3.40 adult; 2015-2016 6-12 Lunch Price $2.65 student / $3.40 adult; 2015-2016 6-12 Lunch Price $3.65 / $3.65; 2015-2016 6-12 Lunch Price $3.90 / $4.90.

Under Other, Dr. Machesky gave a bond projects update; Mr. Schmidt asked about recent flooding at Troy High School in the theatre area from the temporary roofing, and Dr. Machesky said only minor damage occurred and Barton Malow was replacing carpeting and other necessary items. A resolution moved by Mrs. Fleming and supported by Mr. Schmidt adopted the revised schedule of Board meetings for the remainder of the 2015 calendar year, 5-0. Student representatives reported: Maya Adams (Niles Community High School) on the Niles 5K Walk for Clean Water for Lebanon Schools, a Student Council blood drive, a third annual spring cleanup day, and 51 students graduating, nearly half having earned college credits at OCC through Dual Enrollment; Avi Kumar (International Academy-East) on graduation at the Detroit Opera House where IA-East had 108 seniors from the Troy School District walk across the stage, and $17 million in scholarships awarded collectively across all three campuses; Dahlia Ibrahim (Athens) on the "Under the Stars" movie night; and Snigdha Suvarna (Troy High) on the end of AP testing and softball Regionals. Mrs. Fleming noted the TFEE Golf Outing on June 19th; Dr. Machesky noted Troy had 108 students graduate at the International Academy ceremony and that Athens and Troy High graduations were that weekend, followed by Niles graduation on June 10th; Dr. Philippart announced the June 16th Board Workshop preceded by a special meeting for closed session and that the last televised meeting of the summer would be June 23rd. The meeting adjourned at 8:55 p.m. Minutes submitted by Paula Fleming, Secretary, Troy Board of Education (PF/jh).

JUNE 16, 2015 SPECIAL MEETING (Administration Building). Called to order at 5:30 p.m. by President Philippart with Edmunds, Fleming, Hauff, Miletti, Schmidt and Underwood present, and administrators Machesky, Mark Dziatczak, Mary Haezebrouck, Larry Lobert and Rick West. Resolution 15.061, moved by Mr. Hauff and supported by Mr. Schmidt, issued a two-year probationary administrative contract without tenure to Ms. Kristine Griffor as Assistant Superintendent, Elementary Instruction, effective July 1, 2015 (YES 7, NO 0). Resolution 15-062, moved by Mr. Hauff and supported by Mrs. Fleming, approved the personnel recommendation for Director of ELD, Federal Grants and State Assessments (Silagy), 7-0. A motion by Mrs. Fleming supported by Mr. Miletti ratified and adopted the tentative agreement reached on June 5th, 2015 between representatives of the Troy Board of Education and the Troy Educational Support Personnel Association/MEA/NEA for the period July 1, 2015 through June 30, 2016, 7-0. Resolution 15-063, moved by Mr. Schmidt and supported by Ms. Underwood, took the Board into closed session under the Michigan Open Meetings Act, Public Act 267, Section 8(c) to discuss the Superintendent Evaluation; the roll call recorded Hauff, Miletti, Philippart, Schmidt, Underwood, Edmunds and Fleming all voting Yes, motion carried 7-0. The Board moved to closed session at 5:43 p.m. and the meeting reconvened at 5:45 p.m.; on Mr. Hauff's motion the meeting adjourned at 7:30 p.m.

JUNE 16, 2015 CLOSED SESSION. Called to order at 5:30 p.m. with Dr. Philippart, Mrs. Edmunds, Mrs. Fleming, Mr. Hauff, Mr. Miletti, Mr. Schmidt and Ms. Underwood present along with Superintendent Machesky and no one else. Discussion was held regarding Dr. Machesky's evaluation for the 2014-2015 school year; no other business was conducted. Adjourned at 7:30 p.m.

JUNE 16, 2015 BOARD WORKSHOP. Called to order at 7:36 p.m. with all seven members present; administrators Machesky, Ms. Birmingham, Mr. Dziatczak, Mrs. Haezebrouck, Mr. Carson and Mr. West attended along with approximately 20 other members of the audience. The agenda listed public communication, an Innovations presentation, a Summer Success Academy update for Grades 3 and 6, a Michigan Merit Curriculum update, a district property update, and a budget update covering millage renewal, the 2014/2015 final budget amendment and the 2015/2016 budget. Adjourned at 11:05 p.m.

PERSONNEL (6). A. New hire recommendation for a probationary contract for 2015-2016: Michael Denyes, 1.0 FTE Counselor, Smith/Boulan Park Middle Schools. His biographical sketch dated July 7, 2015 lists a B.A. from Oakland University, Rochester, May 2010, majoring in Psychology and Anthropology; an M.A. from Oakland University, December 2012, in School Counseling; a Michigan School Counselor Certificate issued January 2013; service as Counselor at Holly Area Schools, Holly, MI from August 2013 to June 2015; Guest Counselor with PESG, Caledonia, MI from February 2013 to June 2013; resident community Troy, Michigan. B. Superintendent's contract extension. The Board reported that Dr. Richard Machesky completed his first year as a HIGHLY EFFECTIVE superintendent, meeting or exceeding expectations in all evaluation categories, having articulated a clear vision and launched the concept of One Troy, introduced a customer service mindset into Central Office, engaged the community, kept the district fiscally strong, successfully negotiated all labor contracts and filled staff positions. The Board authorized a $5000 bonus and, consistent with average total compensation increases for other staff groups, a 3.5% base salary increase, with the contract extended through June 30, 2018. The suggested resolution states the contract will be in effect from July 1, 2015 through June 30, 2018, without tenure in the administrative position and subject to the provisions of the written Agreement.

CURRICULUM (7). A. Michigan High School Athletic Association membership resolution for 2015/2016, enrolling the six (6) secondary schools under the direction of the Troy Board of Education, City of Troy, County of Oakland, as members of the MHSAA, a voluntary nonprofit corporation, and enrolling them to participate in approved interschool athletic activities; the authorization is effective from August 1, 2015 until July 31, 2016 and may not be revoked during that period. The Board delegates supervision and control to the Superintendent or designee and adopts the MHSAA Constitution, By-Laws and current HANDBOOK rules as minimum standards. B. High School Cooperative Team Agreement: the District seeks MHSAA approval to operate a cooperative team in Boys' Ice Hockey with Athens and Troy High Schools, Troy High as the primary school and Athens as the secondary, for the 2015-16 and 2016-17 school years. C. Athletic Code of Conduct, reviewed at the annual "Vision" meeting, with the revised Code of Conduct for Student Athletes attached (Revised December 2004; Revised July 2015) and to be posted on the District website once approved. The Code contains twelve sections. Section I eligibility requires enrollment by the Monday of the fourth week of the semester; high school participants must be under nineteen (19) years of age, seventh and eighth graders under fourteen (14) and fifteen (15) respectively; a physical examination by an M.D., D.O., physician's assistant or nurse practitioner taken after April 15 of the previous school year; a maximum of four (4) seasons of a sport and four (4) first semesters and four (4) second semesters in grades nine through twelve; and academic eligibility requiring passing grades in a minimum of five (5) classes (Niles 4 classes, Intersect 5 classes, IA 6 of 8 classes), with transfer students new to the district meeting the MHSAA minimum of four (4) classes. Section II limits awards to symbolic or merchandise items not exceeding twenty-five dollars ($25.00) in fair market value and bars cash or negotiable documents. Section III on amateur status applies to baseball, basketball, cross country, football, golf, gymnastics, soccer, softball, skiing, tennis, track, volleyball, wrestling, ice hockey, competitive cheer, swimming and diving. Section IV on outside competition imposes ineligibility for a minimum of the next two (2) days of competition for middle school and three (3) days for high school, reflecting Section 13(A) Limited Team Membership of the MHSAA handbook. Sections V through VIII address school attendance, practice attendance, travel to and from away contests, and responsibility for uniforms and equipment. Section IX on tobacco, alcohol and other drugs sets penalties: a first tobacco violation costs a minimum of the next interscholastic event or one week of a season, capped at 10% of regular season contests; a first alcohol or drug violation or second tobacco violation costs two (2) consecutive events or two (2) weeks, capped at 20% of regular season contests, with a mandatory drug workshop consortium at family expense; a second alcohol or drug violation or third tobacco violation brings dismissal from the team, and if less than 50% of the season remains the student is ineligible for the first half (50%) of the next sport, with professional assessment for chemical dependency at a Michigan State Department of Substance Abuse Services approved agency required; a third alcohol or drug violation or fourth tobacco violation brings exclusion from all interscholastic participation for three hundred and sixty-five (365) days; a fourth alcohol or drug violation or fifth tobacco violation forfeits any remaining eligibility in the Troy School District. Seventh and eighth grade athletes are removed from the team on any violation. Sections X and XI cover voluntary summer and off-season programs and supplemental team rules approved by the building principal. Section XII permits appeal within two (2) school days to the building principal, who must convene a meeting within two (2) school days and respond in writing within two (2) school days, with further appeal to the Deputy Superintendent, whose decision is final.

BUSINESS (8). Consideration of office furniture for Boulan Park and Larson Middle Schools. Invitations to bid were sent to seven potential bidders, with two vendors responding. Responses were reviewed by Rob Carson, Director of Maintenance and Operations; Todd Hensley, Purchasing Supervisor; Michelle Kerns, Owners Representative; and Danielle O'Grady, Interior Architect. The suggested resolution awards the bid to Interior Environments in the amount of $94,383.98 as an expenditure of the 2014 Capital Projects Fund. A June 30, 2015 letter from TMP Architecture, Inc. (1191 West Square Lake Road, Bloomfield Hills, Michigan 48302; PH 248.338.4561, FX 248.338.0223) to Mr. Rick West, Assistant Superintendent, Business Services, references TMP Project Nos. 13170 and 13171 for the Boulan Park Middle School Addition and Larson Middle School Addition. Bids were received June 23, 2015 at 1:30 p.m., with Todd Hensley of Troy School District and Danielle O'Grady and Keri Kahn of TMP Architecture present at the opening. The performance bond was omitted from the total bid amount at the direction of Troy School District. TMP recommended awarding Bid Category A (Hon) to Interior Environments at $91,794.32, Bid Category B (Bailey Manufacturing Company, Inc.) to Interior Environments at $1,249.96, and Bid Category C (Peter Pepper) to Interior Environments at $1,339.70, for a total bid amount of $94,383.98. A July 7, 2015 memorandum from Todd Hensley, Purchasing Supervisor (Purchasing Department, 1440 Rankin, Troy, Michigan 48093; Phone 248 823-4091, Fax 248 823-4013) to Rick West, referencing BID 9812 and the 2013 Bond Project - Series 1, states that questioning of potential bidders revealed the furniture and manufacturer specified did not leave enough margins above current consortium pricing, and recommends the low bidder to specification, Interior Environments, at $94,383.98, funded by the 2014 Capital Projects Fund, with a copy to Pat Orczykowski of the Business Department. The attached bid tabulation, dated bid June 9, 2015 and bid opening June 23, 2015 at 1:30 PM, lists solicited firms including Interior Environments (48700 Grand River Ave., Novi, MI 48374, Attn: Steve Cojei), OM Workspace/Office Depot (17335 Haggerty Road, Northville, MI 48168, Attn: Iwona Buscani), School Specialty, Inc. (100 Paragon Parkway, Mansfield, OH 44903, Attn: Elisa Race), Kentwood Office Furniture (40500 Grand River, Novi, MI 48375, Attn: Bob Hogan), Office Express (1280 E Big Beaver Rd. Ste. A, Troy, MI 48083, Attn: Carol Miller), NBS Commercial Interiors (2595 Bellingham, Troy, MI 48083, Attn: Natalie Kosnik) and American Interiors (30553 S. Wixom Rd., Wixom, MI 48393, Attn: Jen Malia). The tabulation shows a second Bid Category A price of $93,624.16 alongside the recommended $91,794.32, performance bond figures of $1,836.00 and $752.00 for Category A, $25.00 for Category B and $27.00 for Category C, and a grand total award of $94,383.98. Both responding bidders submitted familial disclosure statements, non-collusion affidavits and Iran Economics Sanctions Act certifications, one with a certified check and one with a bid bond.
